chapterTag.category: AP Calc AB Unit 8 — Applications of Integration

body.en: Definite integrals measure areas between curves, volumes of solids, and average values.

Area between curves: \( \displaystyle\int(\text{top}-\text{bottom})\,dx \). Volumes by disks/washers about an axis. Average value: \( \dfrac{1}{b-a}\displaystyle\int_a^b f \). Solids with known cross-sections integrate the section area.

caption.en: The region bounded between $y = x$ and $y = x^2$ on $[0,1]$ has area $\int_0^1 (x - x^2)\,dx = \frac{1}{6}$. The top curve is $y = x$ and the bottom curve is $y = x^2$.

body.en:
Find the area between \( y=x \) and \( y=x^{2} \) on \( [0,1] \).

\[ \int_0^1\big(x-x^{2}\big)\,dx=\frac12-\frac13=\frac16. \]

Find the volume of the solid formed by revolving \(y=\sqrt{x}\) about the \(x\)-axis on \([0,4]\).

\[V=\pi\int_0^4(\sqrt{x})^2\,dx=\pi\int_0^4 x\,dx=\pi\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^4=\pi\cdot8=8\pi.\]

label.en: ⚠ Common traps — Washer radius squaring & average value denominator

body.en:
Square each radius individually: In the washer method, volume is \( \pi \int (R^2 - r^2)\,dx \), NOT \( \pi \int (R - r)^2\,dx \). Subtracting radii before squaring calculates the volume of an entirely different, incorrect solid.

Revolving around lines other than the axes: When revolving around \( y = k \), the radius is \( \text{distance} = |y_{\text{curve}} - k| \). Never assume the radius is simply \( f(x) \) when the axis of rotation has shifted!

Average value vs average rate of change: Average value of \( f \) on \( [a, b] \) is \( \dfrac{1}{b - a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx \). Average rate of change of \( f \) on \( [a, b] \) is \( \dfrac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a} \). Mixing up these two definitions is a frequent loss of points on both MC and FRQ sections.

question.en: The base of a solid is the region in the \(xy\)-plane enclosed by the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 4\). Cross sections perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis are squares. Find the volume of the solid.

solution.en:
For any \(x \in [-2, 2]\), the top boundary of the circle is \(y = \sqrt{4 - x^2}\) and the bottom is \(y = -\sqrt{4 - x^2}\). The side length of the square cross section is:

\[ s(x) = 2\sqrt{4 - x^2}. \]

The area of each square cross section is:

\[ A(x) = [s(x)]^2 = 4(4 - x^2) = 16 - 4x^2. \]

Integrating along the \(x\)-axis from \(-2\) to \(2\):

\[ V = \int_{-2}^2 (16 - 4x^2)\,dx = 2 \int_0^2 (16 - 4x^2)\,dx = 2\left[16x - \frac{4}{3}x^3\right]_0^2 = 2\left(32 - \frac{32}{3}\right) = 2\left(\frac{64}{3}\right) = \frac{128}{3}. \]
